GENERAL NOTES — PHASING, BLOCKS AND OPEN SPACE
1. BLOCKS. Site Development Plan Review Checklist §4.i: "Subdivision — add number of lots/units
… Lot and Block Numbers if applicable. Phasing is not permitted unless platted in Blocks." Block
A (Phase 1, 24 lots) and Block B (Phase 2, 17 lots) are platted as blocks, and every block
boundary drawn here lies on a lot line or a tract line. Numbers A-1…A-24 and B-1…B-17 carry to
the plat; column 2 of each schedule gives the C-2.0 lot number.
2. PHASE LINE. STA 10+34.48 along the travelled way from the Arcado Rd right-of-way (204-ft
entry drive plus lane) = local station u 980. NE side: the common lot line of Lots A-24 and B-5.
SW side: the tract line between Tract E (Pond 1) and Lot B-1. Between them it crosses only the
private lane tract. IT DIVIDES 0 LOTS.
3. PHASE 1 IS DESIGNED TO STAND ALONE. Block A carries the entrance, the entire amenity block
(Tract A), Pond 1 (Tract E), the first turnaround (Tract B) and 24 of the 41 lots, served by
gravity to the existing 8-in county main already crossing the property (MH inv 927.13). No sewer
extension, no off-site easement, no second access; complete whether or not Phase 2 is built.
4. PHASE 2 CONDITION. No Phase 2 work and no land-disturbance permit until (a) the off-site
sewer easement for the ≈ 178-ft gravity tie to the Legends at Parkview main (MH inv 919.58) is
RECORDED and (b) Gwinnett County DWR has issued its SEWER CAPACITY CERTIFICATION (condition 16).
Gravity only: no private pump station, force main, private gravity sewer, grinder pump or
low-pressure system (Gwinnett DWR Standard Policy for Private Developments, rev. 9/2018; WSR-24
§1.3.1(A)). If either fails, Phase 2 is not built, and 4535 Arcado Rd — which stands on the lane
alignment — comes down under permit first (condition 15).
5. OPEN SPACE IS VOLUNTARY. Table 4.1 refers the R-2 open-space requirement to §5.9 of the
Development Regulations; §5.9.1 "Recreation Areas" reaches detached subdivisions "having a gross
area of 50 acres or more." At 9.44 ac it is not engaged: none of the 141,089 SF is required.
6. BUFFER EASEMENT — REPORTED SEPARATELY. The rear 20 ft of each of the 41 lots is undisturbed
buffer in a recorded easement inside the private lot (Ord. 2023-603 §313(1)): 41,000 SF. It is
not a common tract, is not in the 141,089 SF total, and is in no percentage on this sheet.
7. AREA BASIS. 417,174 SF = 9.577 ac GIS; 411,206 SF = 9.44 ac deeded; percentages given against
both. Tract areas are the published residual — GIS area less lots less the lane and entry-drive
tracts — so the eight sum exactly. Tract A is NET: its outline encloses ≈ 58,956 SF, of which ≈
12,164 SF is entry drive and lane tract.
8. BUILT AND PAVED INSIDE THE OPEN SPACE. 13,960 SF of 141,089 SF; the balance, 127,129 SF
(30.5% of the GIS area), is green. Turnaround legs are counted at the full 1,200 SF each
although only ≈ 6,041 SF of the 7,200 SF really falls inside the greens, so the figure is
conservative. The 12 guest and kiosk spaces (2,070 SF of bays) lie in the lane tract and are not
9. MAINTENANCE (§4.o). A mandatory HOA owns and maintains Tracts A–H, the lane tract and its
sidewalks, both ponds, the buffers and buffer easements, the entry sign and the lighting, and
provides yard maintenance to every lot (condition 10). NOTHING IS OFFERED FOR DEDICATION TO THE
CITY; only the sanitary mains and their easements become public, to Gwinnett DWR.
10. NOT SHOWN, AND SOURCES. Dwellings, driveways and setback envelopes — Sheets C-2.0/2.1/2.2;
bearings and topography — C-1.0; grading — C-3.0; utilities — C-4.0/4.1. Only the sewer reaches
on or adjoining the property are drawn. Every area, count and station here is read at run time
